A.explanation: Too small. $2 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ would make the separation speed only $0 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, which is less than the $6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ approach speed.

B.explanation: Too small. $4 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ would give separation speed $2 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, so kinetic energy and relative speed would not be conserved.

C.explanation: Incorrect. $6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ would give separation speed $4 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, which does not equal the $6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ speed of approach.

D.explanation: Correct. $8 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ gives separation speed $8-2 = 6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, equal to the approach speed for a perfectly elastic collision.

hints: Notice the given speeds along the line of impact: X approaches Y at $6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, Y is initially $0 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, and X leaves at $2 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ in the same forward direction.
Connect perfectly elastic to relative speed: speed of approach of the two spheres must equal speed of separation along the same line.
Set the approach $6-0$ equal to the separation $v_Y - 2$ in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ and solve for the unknown speed of Y.
walkthrough: Identify the motion along the collision line. Before: $u_X = 6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ and $u_Y = 0 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$. After: $v_X = 2 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ in the same direction, and $v_Y$ is unknown forward.
State the perfectly elastic rule for head-on impact: speed of approach equals speed of separation.
Calculate speed of approach $= u_X - u_Y = 6 - 0 = 6 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
Write speed of separation $= v_Y - v_X = v_Y - 2$ in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$, because Y must move ahead of X after impact.
Equate them: $v_Y - 2 = 6$, so $v_Y = 8 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$. This is option D.
